page: The UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-32xCPU-256GB is a Cloud Native family virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor with 32 vCPUs and 32 physical cores operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The CPU allocation is shared, and the system is configured with 1.0 thread per core. It is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 8.0 GB of RAM per core. No local storage or GPU hardware is bundled with this instance, though it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates a clear contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is relatively low, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance scoring in the bottom 10%. However, multi-core execution is robust, with Geekbench multi-core, bzip3 multi-threaded decompression, and Passmark CPU physics tests all scoring in the top 25%. Cryptographic operations are also strong, supported by hardware-accelerated AES and SHA instructions. Memory bandwidth remains average, measuring 99.45 GB/sec for large block read-only operations and 44.93 GB/sec for large block write operations.

The shared CPU allocation presents a potential tradeoff for workloads requiring sustained, predictable single-core performance. However, the high memory capacity of 256.0 GB combined with 32 cores makes this server highly cost-efficient for memory-intensive, parallelizable tasks. It is well-suited for large-scale data processing, multi-threaded decompression, memory-cached database operations, and moderate LLM inference tasks, such as prompt processing with 7B or 70B models.
